---
targetPath: /multi-country/brazil_peru/interests/food-and-wine/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore the food of Brazil and Peru"
lead: >-
  Brazil and Peru are connected by a 20-day journey through six South American countries. In Rio de Janeiro and Lima, travelers can discover distinct national culinary traditions, but the published itinerary does not specify dedicated gastronomic excursions in either country. A visit to wineries in the Maipo Valley is offered as an optional excursion in Chile, while a tango dinner is part of the program in Argentina. Compare the geography and inclusions to choose a trip for what it actually offers.
---

## The food of Brazil and Peru within a six-country journey

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} including Brazil and Peru with the “Food and Wine” interest. The current [“6 Latin American Countries in 20 Days: From Rio to Machu Picchu” program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, and Bolivia. Its 2026 schedule gives the dates **October 23 to November 11**.

This type of trip has a particular character. Travelers encounter the food of several regions of the continent, rather than taking part in a single specialist culinary tour devoted to Brazil and Peru. Many days are occupied by flights, sightseeing, historic sites, and a journey across Bolivia's high-altitude landscapes.

The food interest applies to the **entire itinerary**. In particular, there is a tango evening with dinner in Buenos Aires, and travelers can add a separate winery excursion in Chile. These experiences cannot be presented as tastings included in the Brazilian or Peruvian stages.

| Country and stage | Culinary context |
|---|---|
| Brazil, Rio | Opportunities to discover Brazilian dishes between sightseeing excursions |
| Argentina, Buenos Aires | Tango show with dinner in the itinerary |
| Chile, Maipo Valley | Optional wine excursion at additional cost |
| Peru, Lima and Cusco | Famous culinary regions; no separate cooking class specified in the itinerary |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026}}

If your main aim is daily tastings, markets, and time with chefs, discuss adapting the program from the outset. The existing itinerary offers a different travel format: an introduction to several countries with culinary discoveries along the way.

## Rio de Janeiro: trying Brazilian cuisine between excursions

The first days are spent in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The sightseeing program includes city panoramas, Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado, historic neighborhoods, and major architectural landmarks. Travelers then continue to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) to see the waterfalls.

Brazilian cuisine offers many options for independent exploration: rice and beans, cassava, fish, meat, fresh fruit drinks, and regional street food. Feijoada, for example, is one of the country's best-known dishes, based on beans and meat products. However, **no particular restaurant, feijoada cooking class, or local-drink tasting is confirmed as an included service** on the Brazilian days.

A restaurant evening has to fit around sightseeing and transfer times. The published schedule gives no basis for promising a particular food market, tasting menu, or meeting with a cook.

The Iguaçu stage has a nature-focused itinerary. Time is devoted to waterfall excursions and possible nature-related additions, not a prepaid gastronomic program.

For specifically Brazilian culinary experiences, explore [food and wine tours in Brazil](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/brazil/) and consider which extra activities would genuinely fit the travel dates.

## Argentina and Chile: from tango dinner to Maipo wine

After Iguaçu, travelers reach Buenos Aires. The day's description includes a tango show with dinner, one of the few clearly identified culinary experiences of the extended route. Argentina also includes an excursion to Uruguay, so flights and ferry journeys occupy part of the schedule.

The journey then continues to Santiago de Chile. Here, the program separately offers a visit to wineries in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) with tasting. This is **an optional paid excursion**: the published tour price is **$230 per person with a minimum of 2 participants**. It must not be added to the included services or described as a tasting in Brazil or Peru.

Why does this matter? A page filtering for two countries can show a tour with six main countries and the “Food and Wine” theme. The label applies to the overall journey, not an even distribution of tastings across its stages. That makes the [general selection of multi-country food and wine trips](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) useful for comparing what each route actually contains.

## Peru: Lima and Cusco, where history meets cuisine

On the Peruvian section, travelers arrive at Lake Titicaca and then continue to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The final stage is in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

Peruvian cuisine is known for combining Andean ingredients, coastal fish and seafood, and traditions shaped by Indigenous peoples and migrant communities. Ceviche and tiradito are characteristic of Lima: both use raw fish, but differ in preparation, cutting, and sauces. In the highlands, potatoes, corn, and local grains feature more prominently.

The published Peruvian itinerary, however, concentrates on sightseeing: Titicaca, Cusco's archaeological sites, Machu Picchu, and Lima. It **does not specify a separate food-market excursion in Lima or a prepaid tasting dinner in Cusco**. The dishes mentioned here describe regional cuisine, not a guaranteed package menu.

If restaurants and meals are important to you, choose in advance between a free evening at a restaurant, a market excursion, and a cooking activity. Each requires separate agreement on time and terms.

## Through Bolivia: how geography affects meals

Between Chile and Peru, the route crosses Bolivia by off-road vehicle. It includes lagoons, geothermal areas, the Uyuni Salt Flat, La Paz, and ancient Tiwanaku. The experience is entirely different from an evening at a restaurant in a major city.

The high-altitude section requires attention to wellbeing and drinking water. The rhythm of restaurant evenings cannot be carried over into every day of a road expedition. If you have dietary restrictions, discuss meals in remote areas beforehand, where the choice of supplies and establishments can differ from Rio or Lima.

The program also includes domestic flights and transfers. Even if you want to try several local dishes in a particular city, the timetable must leave genuine time to do so.

## Turning an interest in both cuisines into a travel plan

When planning with Ada Tours, first determine your priority: food as an enjoyable addition to a larger sightseeing itinerary, or cuisine as the journey's main purpose. The answer affects the route, number of nights in each city, and supplementary services.

For a cultural and nature-focused trip, you might choose dishes of interest in advance, discuss dietary requirements, and leave free evenings in Rio and Lima. For a specialist journey, markets, tastings, encounters with local cooks, and wineries can be discussed separately. Their inclusion must be confirmed before payment, rather than inferred from a category name on the site.

Compare all current programs featuring both countries on the [Brazil + Peru page](/multi-country/brazil_peru/). Separate [food and wine trips in Peru](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/peru/) and [tours in Brazil](/brazil/tour/) show how the balance of sightseeing and restaurant days can change.

## Frequently asked questions about the cuisines of Brazil and Peru

### Is a Peruvian cuisine tasting included in the price?

The description of the 20-day tour does not list a separate tasting excursion or fixed gastronomic menu in Peru. Mentioning local dishes in an article does not make them a paid-for service.

### Is there a winery on the route?

A visit to wineries in Chile's Maipo Valley is offered separately for **$230 per person, minimum 2 participants**, according to the published itinerary. This is not an included tasting in Brazil or Peru.

### Can this itinerary be described as a Brazil-and-Peru-only tour?

No. It visits six countries: Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, and Peru. The intersection highlights two countries within the full route.

### What should I choose if local food is my main goal?

Discuss an individual itinerary with confirmed gastronomic experiences. The group tour described is designed primarily as a broad introduction to South America's cities, landscapes, and history.

targetPath: /multi-country/brazil_peru/interests/nature/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore nature tours in Brazil and Peru"
lead: >-
  Brazil and Peru bring together Iguaçu Falls, humid subtropical forest, the high Andes, valleys around Cusco, and Lake Titicaca. Their itineraries differ in how many days remain for nature after city visits and flights. Compare the waterfall stage, high-altitude stops, and the full geography: many of the trips in this selection also visit Argentina.
---

## Brazil and Peru: waterfalls, rainforest, and the Andes

The natural attractions of [Brazil](/brazil/) and [Peru](/peru/) are strikingly different. On the Brazilian stage, travel often centers on [Iguaçu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where torrents plunge into a gorge amid Atlantic Forest. In Peru, the route ascends from the Pacific coast toward the Andes, home to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and high-altitude [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/).

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. All these itineraries feature both countries, but some also pass through Argentina, Chile, and other stops. **The nature-focused character of a tour depends on the actual days at the waterfalls, in the mountains, and by the lake**, not how many countries appear in the title. The full selection is in the [Brazil and Peru combination catalog](/multi-country/brazil_peru/).

## Iguaçu: understanding the waterfall excursion

From Foz do Iguaçu on the Brazilian side, travelers see a wide panorama of the cascades. Humid air, spray, and the surrounding forest form an entirely different environment from Peru's highlands. The Iguaçu national parks also protect remnants of Atlantic Forest, but a visit to the viewpoints is not a guaranteed wildlife-watching excursion.

Check **which side of the waterfalls is included** in the particular tour. The Brazilian and Argentine sides are in separate countries and have different visiting arrangements. For example, the [14-day journey through Brazil, Argentina, and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) includes both sides, with Argentina as one of the main countries. An optional boat ride or helicopter excursion is not included merely because it is available near the falls.

On the [“Machu Picchu, Brazil and Rio Beaches” tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/), the journey moves from the Peruvian mountains to Iguaçu, Rio de Janeiro, and Búzios. The nature experiences are combined with beach time, so choose it with the ocean stay in mind, rather than expecting additional hikes in forest.

## Peru: mountain valleys, Titicaca, and the environment of Machu Picchu

The Peruvian section of these journeys often runs through Cusco and Machu Picchu. The archaeological complex stands among steep green slopes at the transition between the high Andes and humid mountain forests. **A visit to Machu Picchu is primarily a cultural and historical excursion:** the mountains make it spectacular, but admission to the ruins does not in itself mean a separate nature trek.

Some programs add Lake Titicaca, with its very different landscape of high-altitude water, open spaces, and islands. The [Peru and Brazil tour with a beach extension](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) includes Puno and a trip to the Uros Islands. The [14-day Brazil, Argentina, and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) likewise has a Peruvian section through Cusco and Puno.

Travelers gain altitude between these stops. Because of the substantial difference between low-lying cities and the Andes, Cusco and Puno require a measured pace, rather than an overfilled schedule immediately after a flight. If Peru's landscapes are your primary goal, compare [nature tours in Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/) without necessarily adding the distant Brazilian section.

## Comparing current itineraries

| Itinerary | Principal emphasis |
|---|---|
| Peru + Brazil | Titicaca, Iguaçu, beaches |
| Brazil + Argentina + Peru, 14 days | Both sides of Iguaçu, Andes |
| Group itinerary, 15 days | Iguaçu, Machu Picchu, glacier |

The [15-day group “Brazil, Peru, and Argentina” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) passes through Foz do Iguaçu, Cusco, and Machu Picchu before continuing to El Calafate. The glacier day takes place **in Argentina**, not in Peru's nature program. This is a key difference when comparing scenery with a trip ending on Brazilian beaches.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_tur_v_peru_i_braziliyu,tour_brazil_argentina_peru_14d,tour_brazil_peru_argentina_group_15_days}}

Some travelers want to see waterfalls and archaeological monuments without a long expedition; others seek several distinct natural regions and are happy to add a third country. Look at the actual day sequence, domestic flights, overnight altitudes, and separately listed excursions. Paying for a longer journey should provide meaningful additional days on location.

## Seasons, flights, and preparation

Iguaçu has a humid subtropical climate; the strength of the flow and walking conditions change with rainfall. Peru's Andes follow different weather patterns: the rainy season affects mountain trails and visibility, while mornings can be cold even on clear days. There is no meaningful single promise of “perfect weather” in both countries.

Pack protection against rain and spray at the waterfalls, footwear with a good grip, and clothes for cool mountain conditions. When moving from Rio or Lima to Cusco, consider not only flight duration but also the altitude of subsequent stops. People with health conditions affected by elevation should discuss their planned exertion with a doctor.

Travel combining both countries often requires several distinct flights. Before booking, establish which flights are included in the specific price, how many nights are allocated to the main sights, and which countries a flight or land transfer passes through. Entry and transit requirements differ by citizenship; check the complete itinerary, including Argentina when it features in the program.

For nature-focused stops in Brazil, there is the [country's nature tour catalog](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/). For encounters with animals, choose [“Wildlife and Safari”](/interests/wildlife/): having forest around Iguaçu or mountains near Machu Picchu does not prove that a particular wildlife-watching activity is scheduled.

## Frequently asked questions about nature tours in Brazil and Peru

### Do all the tours visit Iguaçu Falls?

Several itineraries in the selection include Iguaçu, but check the exact tour. Visits to both sides and optional activities need separate confirmation.

### Is Machu Picchu a nature excursion?

It is primarily a historical and archaeological monument in a remarkable mountain setting. If you want nature walks, confirm their specific inclusion, duration, and access conditions.

### Which is more demanding: Iguaçu or the Peruvian highlands?

They place different demands on travelers. At Iguaçu, paths, humidity, and heat matter; in Cusco and Puno, altitude gain and acclimatization are more significant. Actual difficulty depends on the day and the traveler.

### Can I combine Iguaçu and Lake Titicaca?

Yes. Both are included, for instance, in the [Machu Picchu, Iguaçu, and Brazilian coast itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/). Consider the length of transfers between the regions.

targetPath: /multi-country/brazil_peru/interests/wildlife/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore wildlife watching on journeys through Brazil and Peru"
lead: >-
  On journeys through Brazil and Peru, nature experiences change from humid forests around Iguaçu Falls to the mountain valleys of Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca. But a nature-focused trip does not necessarily include dedicated wildlife watching. Birds at waterfalls, Andean wildlife, and a separate Amazon expedition are different activities. We explain which places are actually included in the multi-country programs and how to choose without inflated expectations.
---

## Brazil and Peru: the landscapes connected by these journeys

**The most noticeable contrast between the two countries on these routes is the shift from humid subtropical forest to the high Andes.** Brazilian days often feature [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), while the Peruvian stages include [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/).

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries as main destinations and the “Wildlife and Safari” interest. **The theme applies to the entire tour.** It does not prove that independent safaris are planned in both countries, that rare animals can be seen every day, or that an Amazon expedition is included.

For the full country combinations, use the [Brazil + Peru catalog](/multi-country/brazil_peru/). Other country combinations featuring wildlife experiences appear in the [multi-country “Wildlife and Safari” selection](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/).

## Brazil: Iguaçu, Atlantic Forest, and incidental sightings

At [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the principal attractions are the waterfalls and forest paths of the national park. Travelers hear the powerful water, experience the humid forest, and may see birds near the paths. Iguaçu forms part of a natural system on the Argentine border; visiting the Brazilian side and Argentina's [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) requires the route and countries to be considered separately.

As a comparison of scenic trips, the [14-day “Brazil, Argentina, and Peru” tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) includes both sides of Iguaçu before continuing to Peru's cities and monuments. It offers waterfalls and Andean landscapes, but in itself **does not guarantee sightings of a jaguar, tapir, or other rare animals** living in protected forests.

Some programs around Iguaçu offer the [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) or a separate boat trip at the falls. **The Bird Park and the boat excursion have different purposes**, and additional activities may cost extra. Their availability in the region does not make them included in every tour: check the particular day.

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the road to Corcovado passes through Tijuca Forest. The [15-day group journey through Brazil, Peru, and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) mentions the possibility of seeing monkeys and exotic birds along the way, but this is **a chance encounter**, not an excursion promising to find them.

## Peru: nature around Inca monuments and the high-altitude lake

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) stands on the eastern slopes of the Andes among montane forest. Its natural setting is part of the experience, but on most itineraries under consideration the excursion's primary purpose is to see the archaeological complex. Without confirmation of a separate program, a Machu Picchu visit should not be treated as a specialist search for rare wildlife.

Another Peruvian landscape is high-altitude [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). On the Peru and Brazil tour with a beach extension, the route begins in Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, and Titicaca before continuing to Brazilian Iguaçu, Rio, and the coast. The lake adds a different elevation and ecosystem, but visiting the floating reed islands primarily concerns local communities' culture rather than a safari.

The [15-day New Year tour through Brazil and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-new-year/) includes the desert coast of Paracas and the Nazca Lines region. On day 14, there is an included sea excursion of approximately **2 hours** to islands off Paracas, which are inhabited by Humboldt penguins, sea lions, and birds. This included visit is a genuine reason to choose the trip for watching wild animals, although sightings of particular species are not guaranteed.

**A separate Amazon expedition** has a different duration, transport, and program from the familiar route through Cusco and Machu Picchu. This page addresses confirmed nature stages on the selected multi-country tours; for an Amazon experience, choose only an itinerary explicitly including that section.

## Choosing according to a specific nature experience

| Travel goal | What to check |
|---|---|
| Iguaçu Falls | Days and border sides |
| Andean landscapes | Overnight stops and elevations |
| Birds and animals | Dedicated excursions |
| Peruvian coast | Specific boat outings |

Compare the actual programs:

The table below compares itineraries that include opportunities to watch wild animals or birds. Scenic journeys without such activities can be compared in the [nature travel selection](/multi-country/brazil_peru/interests/nature/). On a multi-country tour, wildlife watching may take place beyond the countries in the selection title: check the entire route and the particular days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_braziliya_i_peru_na_novyj_god,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The [14-day private route through Argentina](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) combines waterfalls and Peru's main cultural attractions. The [15-day group journey](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) adds Perito Moreno Glacier in Argentina. This broadens the nature program, but the glacier is **not in Brazil or Peru**. A [13-day Peru and Brazil itinerary with a beach holiday](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) combines mountains, waterfalls, and the ocean without a required separate jungle expedition.

Some larger eight-country trips include the Galápagos, but those islands are **in Ecuador**. The appearance of such a tour in the Brazil + Peru intersection does not transfer the island excursions to either selected country.

## Weather, seasons, and wildlife

Iguaçu has humid tropical and subtropical conditions, with walkways near waterfall spray. Camera protection and non-slip shoes are useful year-round. Access to individual paths depends on the river and decisions of the national park; all viewpoints cannot be promised for every date.

Weather in the Peruvian Andes varies by altitude and time of day. [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is much higher than Lima, while Machu Picchu and Titicaca differ in humidity and temperature. One journey requires both lightweight clothes for warm Brazil and protection from cold, sun, and rain in mountain Peru.

Wild animals follow their own routines. Sightings depend on time of day, season, excursion route, and human behavior. Even when a species lives within a protected area, an encounter is not guaranteed. For those traveling specifically to watch birds and mammals, dedicated observation days are more meaningful than a park's list of possible fauna.

## Combining nature days and flights

A short overland excursion between [Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is not realistic. The journey normally requires flights with connections specified in the tour; some itineraries also visit Buenos Aires or Lima between these places. Expanding the geography adds time at airports.

High-altitude visits should be planned with attention to wellbeing and gradual acclimatization. Machu Picchu admission and transport, national park transfers, and border procedures must be arranged for the specific date, citizenship, and product. We help choose the sequence and clarify where the program provides wildlife watching rather than scenic walks.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Brazil and Peru

### Can I see wild animals at Iguaçu Falls?

Birds and other animals live in the surrounding forest, but no particular species is guaranteed. The [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) is a separate facility with enclosures, not wild birdwatching in their natural habitat; it may be offered as an extra in the programs discussed.

### Is the Amazon included in every Brazil and Peru tour?

No. A journey through [Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), Rio, Cusco, and Machu Picchu is not the same as an Amazon expedition. That stage must be explicitly included.

### Can I see both the falls and Machu Picchu?

Yes. For example, the [14-day program](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) includes both Iguaçu and Machu Picchu, along with Argentina as the third main country.

### Which tour should I choose for birds?

Look for included wildlife-watching activities: the sea outing near Paracas on the New Year tour, or the Galápagos island excursion on the 32-day itinerary. The Galápagos are in Ecuador. The optional [Bird Park at Iguaçu](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) differs from watching wild birds and does not turn a scenic tour into a safari.

### Where is the climate more challenging?

It depends on season and location. Iguaçu's humid forest, coastal Lima, and high-altitude Cusco require different clothing. Plan for specific cities and dates, not a country's average weather.

targetPath: /multi-country/brazil_peru_uruguay/
kind: multi_country_combination
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore tours through Brazil, Peru, and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Brazil, Peru, and Uruguay are linked within Ada Tours' long itineraries via Iguaçu, Buenos Aires, Montevideo, and the high Andes. On one trip, travelers can see Rio de Janeiro, both sides of the falls, Uruguay's capital, the Uyuni Salt Flat, and Machu Picchu. However, the ready-made programs also pass through Argentina, Chile, and Bolivia. Choosing between them therefore requires attention to the true country order, flights, repeated entries, altitude, and Inca-site tickets.
---

## Brazil, Peru, and Uruguay: what the actual routes include

From coastal [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) lies much of South America, while [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is not on a straight line between them. Travel featuring all three countries therefore calls for careful route planning. The difference between a brief stop and a substantial part of the journey matters more than how many countries are named.

The selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with [Brazil](/brazil/), [Peru](/peru/), and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) as main countries: the [20-day group tour across six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Both visit Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay first, then continue through Chile and Bolivia into Peru. In the 32-day version, the journey continues from Lima to Ecuador and Colombia.

**Neither is a ready-made tour limited to Brazil, Peru, and Uruguay.** The other countries are integral to transport and excursions.

| Stage | What you will see |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio and Iguaçu Falls |
| Uruguay | One-day Montevideo visit |
| Peru | Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Lima |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If you are mainly interested in two countries, compare [Brazil and Peru itineraries](/multi-country/brazil_peru/) or [Brazil and Uruguay](/multi-country/brazil_uruguay/). A private three-country journey would require new flights and omission of intermediate stages while retaining your chosen experiences.

## Brazil: from Rio de Janeiro to both sides of Iguaçu

The 20-day tour begins in Rio. It includes sightseeing, [Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), and Sugarloaf Mountain. Travelers then fly to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The falls become the transition between the Brazilian and Argentine sections.

Geography matters at Iguaçu. The [Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) are in separate countries; visiting both requires transport, admission tickets, and time for border formalities. One panoramic view of the falls does not replace two distinct visits.

The 32-day version also begins with São Paulo before continuing through Rio and both sides of Iguaçu. When comparing the programs, account for this extra city stop rather than assuming a longer overall itinerary necessarily allows more time at the waterfalls.

In Brazil, travelers are mostly at low elevation in a warm climate. Within a few days the nature of the journey changes: after Argentina and Uruguay, the route leads to Chile's Atacama and then Bolivia's and Peru's highlands. Clothes for Rio will serve for only part of the trip.

## Uruguay: how the Montevideo excursion works

On both trips, [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited **on a one-day excursion from Buenos Aires**. Travelers reach the Argentine capital's port, take a ferry across the Río de la Plata, explore the city, and return by ferry to Argentina. The eight-country program expressly includes the ferry tickets, and the six-country program also lists the ferry among paid-for services.

This format introduces another South American capital without changing hotels for several nights. But Uruguay's beach resorts, wine regions, and extended coastal journeys are **not included** in these itineraries. Travelers whose main goal is Uruguay need a more detailed route.

The ferry day depends closely on the timetable in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). Travelers need valid documents **to enter Uruguay and re-enter Argentina**. Confirm the departure, boarding deadline, return ticket, and transfer to the port. Avoid tight connections with a long-distance flight immediately after the ferry unless the full timetable has been confirmed.

In an extended itinerary, Uruguay is a short but distinct cultural stage: the historic center of Montevideo offers a contrast with enormous Rio and the high-altitude cities that follow.

## Why the route from Uruguay to Peru passes through Chile and Bolivia

On a map, Brazil, Uruguay, and Peru might look like three points connected by flights. But **the actual Ada Tours route is different**. After Buenos Aires, the group flies to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), then to Calama and by road to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/).

From Atacama, travelers cross into Bolivia in 4×4 vehicles. The high-altitude stage includes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), hot springs and geothermal areas, other lagoons, and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), and a border crossing into Peru follow.

Between Montevideo and Machu Picchu are several days of their own, long drives, domestic flights, and at least two important land border crossings. They cannot be removed from the published timetable without changing the entire program. If you want more time in Peru and fewer transfers, address that when designing a new private itinerary.

The Bolivian section crosses remote terrain, in places above **4,000 m**. Even brief stops can be tiring. Time to acclimatize, warm clothes, sensible exertion, and insurance covering high altitude are essential. Anyone with a medical condition potentially affected by elevation should discuss the route with a doctor in advance.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu, and Lima

The Peruvian stage begins after the crossing from Bolivia near Desaguadero. Travelers head to [Puno on Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and visit the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). A tourist bus then takes the mountain road to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/).

The next major stop is [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Both current tours include it as a separate excursion day. Cusco's monuments follow, then a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). The six-country tour ends here. In the eight-country version, the journey continues through Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands, and cities in Colombia.

The key to this Peruvian section is **planning Machu Picchu admission in advance**. Official tickets are issued for a chosen date, time, and visiting circuit. Availability on one circuit does not mean another has places. Confirm admission before finalizing the associated trains, hotels, and onward flight.

Travelers should also distinguish high-altitude Cusco from coastal Lima. Even if they have spent several days at altitude in Bolivia, exertion and the pace of transfers remain individual factors. Assess actual opportunities to rest from the day-by-day itinerary.

## Three countries in the heading, six or eight sets of entry requirements

Before booking, check **every country on the actual route**, not just the three in the catalog title. The 20-day journey includes Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, and Peru. The 32-day version also requires up-to-date entry information for Ecuador and Colombia.

Pay particular attention to returning from Montevideo to Argentina, visiting both sides of Iguaçu, and crossing overland from Chile into Bolivia and then into Peru. Each stage may have its own passport rules, entry permissions, requirements for children, transit conditions, and supporting documents. Visa-free travel to one country does not automatically allow entry to the next.

Requirements vary with citizenship. For Russian and other passports, including travelers holding more than one citizenship, check the current rules of the relevant immigration and consular authorities. Re-entry and transit eligibility should be confirmed before purchasing non-refundable tickets. We can help organize the route and questions to check; admission decisions rest with border authorities.

## Seasons and luggage: ocean, waterfalls, and Andes

Brazil's coast, the Iguaçu basin, the Río de la Plata, and the central Andes have different weather. In Rio and Iguaçu, lightweight clothes and protection from sun and rain are useful. On the ferry to Montevideo, consider wind and conditions on the water. Chile, Bolivia, and high-altitude Peru call for insulating layers, a windproof jacket, and shoes suitable for longer stops.

Elevation matters at least as much as temperature. Lowland cities are followed by Altiplano areas where nights can be cold even when Brazil is warm. Rain also affects travel across Uyuni: reflective water and a dry salt crust look different, and access may change with road conditions.

When choosing a season, first identify the journey's main nature attraction. If you dream of a particular appearance of the salt flat, assess Bolivia's weather window; if Machu Picchu matters more, consider Peru's rainy season and ticket availability. There is no universal month offering perfect conditions for every region.

Check baggage allowances separately on domestic flights. Compact luggage and warm clothing deserve particular attention on the jeep section. For a long journey, layered clothing is more practical than one heavy suitcase packed for beaches alone or mountains alone.

Admission is tied to a date, time, and visiting circuit. Changing it may affect train journeys, Cusco excursions, and the onward flight to Lima.

## Which adventures are actually included in these itineraries?

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [20-day journey through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and a [32-day itinerary through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Both include [Brazil](/brazil/), [Uruguay](/uruguay/), and [Peru](/peru/) as main countries. But they are extensive journeys across the continent: Chile and Bolivia lie between Montevideo and Peru, while the 32-day tour continues to Ecuador and Colombia.

Here, adventure mainly means close contact with nature, walking along prepared paths, high-altitude road journeys, and frequent changes of location. **Neither program includes a multi-day walk to Machu Picchu or a separate expedition in Uruguay.** If a sporting hike is important to you, it needs to be discussed as a change to the itinerary.

## Brazil: water, forest, and Iguaçu viewpoints

The first active nature stage begins after sightseeing in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Travelers fly to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and explore the Brazilian side of the falls. They then visit [Iguaçu's Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). The two sides provide different perspectives on the cascades: broad panoramas and closer approaches to falling water.

**Macuco Safari is offered as an optional excursion**, combining a forest ride with a boat trip toward the waterfalls. The Bird Park is also offered separately. These activities must not be treated as included just because they are mentioned in the day's description. For a boat trip, confirm activity restrictions, the likelihood of getting wet, and the time remaining after the main excursion.

Iguaçu suits those wanting to see a powerful river system in subtropical forest without a long unsupported trek. Comfortable non-slip shoes, protection for electronics against spray, and lightweight clothing for humid weather are more useful here than heavy trekking equipment.

## Peru: altitude, Titicaca, and the journey to Machu Picchu

The Peruvian stage starts around [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then continues through mountain valleys toward [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). The scenery, altitude, and transport arrangements change repeatedly. On the lake, a visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) is scheduled, followed by Inca monuments.

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is visited on an organized excursion with a rail section, not on a multi-day hike along the Inca Trail. The monument lies in the mountains, but the principal itinerary is designed for sightseeing. This is an essential distinction when choosing a trip labeled “Adventure.”

The difficulty of the Peruvian section is often determined less by walking distance than by tolerating altitude, early departures, and packed days. Discuss individual high-altitude risks with a doctor before traveling, and be cautious if altitude-sickness symptoms appear. Additional sporting activities should be chosen only after considering how travelers feel following earlier days in the highlands.

## Uruguay: a ferry crossing and city stop

Both programs visit [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) **on a one-day trip from Buenos Aires**, crossing the Río de la Plata by ferry and returning afterward. A city tour covers the capital, port, Independence Square, and Old Town.

This is an interesting change of country and transport, but **no nature-focused or extreme activity is included in the Uruguay day**. Its contribution to the adventure itinerary is an opportunity to see another nation without an extended inland journey. The ferry depends on the operator's timetable and conditions; documents, boarding times, and a buffer for possible delays are particularly important.

For trekking, kayaking, or wildlife watching specifically in Uruguay, neither of these two tours confirms such a specialist program. Decide which activity interests you first and then build a private itinerary around it.

## The most demanding section lies between Uruguay and Peru

After returning from Montevideo, the trip continues through Santiago, [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), and Bolivia's high-altitude regions. This is where the jeep journeys across lagoons and salt flats toward [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) take place, followed by [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and ancient [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/).

Although Chile and Bolivia are absent from this three-country selection's title, **these stages are not optional** in either current program. Removing them changes the sequence, excursions, transport, and duration of the whole journey. Assessing physical demands from Brazil, Peru, and Uruguay alone would therefore be misleading.

At altitude, the speed of ascent and time for acclimatization matter. Sun and wind protection, warm layers, and drinking water are useful in a daypack; preparation should also take account of a doctor's advice. The climate of Rio, the high plateau, and Peruvian valleys cannot be assessed from one country's forecast.

## Choosing between 20 and 32 days

The 20-day tour ends in Lima after all the principal stages of Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, and Peru. It is suited to travelers looking for recognizable natural and historical sites along with a high-altitude jeep section, while keeping the overall calendar shorter.

The 32-day version follows the same geographic framework, then adds Ecuador with the Galápagos and Colombia. The extra time provides more opportunities to experience nature, but increases the number of flights, transfers, and days away from home. In the Galápagos, **one of two alternative sea excursions** is included, not both.

Before choosing, decide what matters most: an intensive introduction to the Andes or a longer expedition across South America. ## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Brazil, Peru, and Uruguay

### Can we hike to Machu Picchu along the Inca Trail?

Neither program includes that multi-day trek. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is visited as a sightseeing attraction; a hiking route would require separate planning for time, permits, and logistics.

### Are there adventure excursions in Uruguay?

In the current tours, Uruguay's day is devoted to the ferry and exploring Montevideo. No specialist outdoor or sports excursion is included there.

### Is Macuco Safari at Iguaçu included in the price?

No. It is an optional activity on both itineraries and must be arranged separately. The main waterfall visit remains included without it.

### What matters most when preparing for altitude?

Discuss health and acclimatization, since the route crosses Bolivia's high plateau toward Peru. Personal limitations should be assessed beforehand, even when travel is by car rather than on foot.

### Can the trip be limited to the three countries in the selection title?

Yes, but that would be a different private program with new flights and duration. The existing 20- and 32-day tours include several other countries as compulsory stages.
